newsitem.title: UK: Stals welcomes rand strength, sees more rises.
newsitem.headline: Stals welcomes rand strength, sees more rises.

text.p: South African Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said on Tuesday he welcomed the rand appreciation of the last few months and predicted more gains this year.
Speaking from South Africa in an interview with Reuters Financial Television, Stals said the currency market had overreacted to his comments earlier in the day which led to a sharp drop in the rand.
"We definitely welcome the appreciation of the rand that took place over the last three months," he said, adding that the gains had only partly cancelled out last year's rand depreciation.
"We have weathered the storm of last year and the exchange rate should remain firm and we could see further appreciation in the coming months."

"Even under the adverse conditions of last year we continued our programme (of exchange control relaxation), so we will certainly continue with that programme and it will not be influenced by small little blips in the market," Stals said.
A stronger rand made it much easier to fight inflation.

"We are confident the inflationary impact of last year's depreciation is gradually beginning to work itself out and that the rate of inflation will gradually come down again to the levels we had early last year," he said.
He said the central bank had been buying dollars on Tuesday.
"We have been buying dollars in the market today," he said.
"The intervention in the market recently has been to absorb surplus dollars."

Earlier, central bank officials said they had been selling dollars to stabilise the rand after it fell sharply on reports quoting Stals as saying that the rand's recent rally could be a slight over-adjustment.
Stals referred to the reports of his remarks as "interpretation" by a financial reporter.
